Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

## Example 1: 2024-09-13 - Price is declining from ~66-73 range
- History: Prices have been declining from 73.07 down to 65.45 (end of the 18-day window)
- Sentiment: Mix of positive (1.00) and negative (0.00, -0.33), mostly positive in middle
- Model forecasts: Start at 65.40 and gradually increase to 64.63 by day 30
- True outcomes: Start at 64.99 and gradually increase to 66.63 by day 30

Looking at the divergence:
- At day 1, model says 65.40 vs true 64.99 (off by +0.41, ~0.6%)
- At day 10, model says 69.60 vs true 66.52 (off by +3.08, ~4.6%)
- At day 20, model says 68.70 vs true 65.00 (off by +3.70, ~5.7%)
- At day 30, model says 64.63 vs true 66.63 (off by -2.00, ~3.0%)

Wait, let me re-examine. The model is forecasting prices that are generally below true prices in this declining environment. But looking more carefully:

Actually, looking at Example 1:
- History ends at 65.45 on day 1, then 64.34, 63.70, etc. - so prices continue declining
- Model forecasts also decline but not as fast

Let me look at the pattern:
Day 1: Model 65.40, True 64.99 (model ~0.6% higher)
Day 5: Model 65.14, True 62.82 (model ~3.7% higher)
